h2: NDT tank inspection in Houston: terminal and plant tanks, and the new Texas tank rules
html:
NDT tank inspection in Houston: terminal and plant tanks, and the new Texas tank rules

Most of Houston's storage tanks are along the Houston Ship Channel, in bulk liquid terminals, refineries and chemical plants between Galena Park and Baytown. NDT tank inspection there means MFL floor scanning, UT shell thickness readings, visual examination and vacuum-box testing for the owner's API 653 program. Atlantis, based in Houston, performs the NDE. The owner's API 653 inspector reviews it and signs the inspection.

How many tanks are involved. The Port Houston complex has more than 200 public and private terminals and ranks first among US ports for foreign waterborne tonnage. One terminal alone can run hundreds of tanks. Kinder Morgan's Galena Park terminal lists 231 tanks on 452 acres, from 5,000 to 187,000 barrels each, holding refined products, chemicals, vegetable oil, ethanol and biodiesel. The product affects the inspection. Floor corrosion rates, internal linings and cleaning needs differ by service. Floor scans are planned around the out-of-service dates the terminal sets for product movements, not around a refinery turnaround.

Texas tank rules since 2023. After the March 2019 fire at the Intercontinental Terminals Company tank farm in Deer Park, the legislature passed Senate Bill 900. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality put it into effect as the Aboveground Storage Vessel Safety program, 30 TAC Chapter 338, on August 24, 2023. It covers non-earthen tanks of 21,000 gallons (500 barrels) or more that store regulated substances at petrochemical plants, refineries and bulk storage terminals. It exempts some categories, such as production and gathering tanks and heated tanks. Registration is due by September 1, 2027, and owners of existing vessels must self-certify compliance by September 1, 2037. Certification is the owner's job. Floor, shell and weld data collected now give the owner evidence to support it later.

Federal overlays. EPA's Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure rule (40 CFR Part 112) expects bulk storage containers to be integrity tested on a schedule set by an industry standard. For welded field-erected tanks, that standard is usually API 653. Where a tank is part of a covered process, OSHA process safety management adds mechanical integrity requirements.

Gulf Coast conditions. Hurricane season runs from June through November. Heavy rain on external floating roofs, blocked roof drains and storm surge into low-lying tank farms mean roof, seal and shell checks are often needed after a storm. Humid, salty air speeds up corrosion at the chime and under insulation on heated tanks, so those areas need more than a quick look during external inspection.

  • Floor plates: MFL tank floor scanning with UT prove-up of each indication
  • Shell courses: UT thickness by course for the minimum-thickness calculation
  • Floor and repair welds: vacuum-box and leak testing
  • Roof, seals, nozzles and foundation: visual records with located photographs

Routing. Most visits here come from general "NDT tank inspection" searches. The national service is on aboveground storage tank inspection, and the split between NDE and the API 653 inspector's role is explained on API 653 tank inspection support. For Texas-wide scopes, see API 653 tank inspection in Texas. Every Houston service is listed on inspection services in Houston. To plan a terminal or plant tank program, use the Houston tank inspection enquiry.
